title: Chapter 586
paragraphs: Chapter 586
Episode 152. Quaul Ganesto (1)
Jin smiled to himself. Although he had started firing the cannon abruptly, it was a moment when it was clear that Quaul was not a person incapable of conversation.
Moreover, answering questions and meeting the conditions that the other person wants were Jin's areas of expertise.
"Let's start with the questions."
"How did you find out I was here?"
"I heard it from Talaris."
"Talaris...?"
Tingjen tilted his head when he heard her name, as if it was the first time he had heard it.
For a moment, Jin and Syris wondered if Quaul was a different person from the Tingjen Talaris had spoken of, but soon he was surprised and said this.
"Oh! Talaris. Yes, Talaris Kendoruma!"
"Isn't it Endorma?"
"Was it Endorma? Right... There was a woman like that..."
Jin, of course, and even Syris, could not help but be dumbfounded by Quaul's reaction, which deepened his gaze as he recalled old memories.
In particular, Syris felt not only discomfort, but also a kind of fresh shock.
Although she had no grudge, Syris had seen quite a few of the many men who had been Talaris' lovers.
All of them clung to his mother pathetically. In severe cases, they threatened to take their own lives if she didn't meet them, but of course, Talaris never extended a hand to such ex-lovers.
Syris had even dealt with serious cases himself, such as those who spread excessive rumors about Talaris or tried to tarnish the image of the Immortal Garden.
Alkaro Chenderra, Talaris's 307th boyfriend when Jin was a middle-class student in Mamit, was also eliminated by Syris.
Jin and Syris first met there.
'Mother... He couldn't even remember her? What kind of person is this? No, is that even possible?'
Even if they weren't lovers, Talaris is a person who is hard to forget once seen.
Ordinary people wouldn't even have a chance to see her, and the unique silver hair and atmosphere of the Endorma clan embody a mystique that cannot be felt from anyone else.
But Quaul seemed to have completely forgotten her. It didn't look like he was pretending to forget at all.
"...No, didn't you already know? The one blocking your cannonballs just now was the Energy of Ice."
The Energy of Ice had a completely different feel from ordinary ice magic. Yet Quaul seemed to have just remembered that too, clapping his hands. There was even a twinkle in his eye.
"Right, come to think of it, that guy uses the same power as Talaris Kendoruma!"
"It's Endorma!"
Syris shouted out loud.
Quaul, either way, continued to look pitiful.
At this point, even Syris was too angry to be upset.
"Oh, Mort. It's been a while since I've seen that guy too. Then you must be her daughter. Nice to meet you. Tingjen Bower."
"Go away."

"And you're her son-in-law, or soon-to-be son-in-law. Thinking about it, I think I heard that there was a marriage proposal going on between the 12th batch of Runcandel and the princess of the Immortal Garden. Is Talaris doing well?"
Just as Jin was considering his response, Quaul shook his head.
"No, ha! Forget it. I'm not interested in past loves."
"Huh, what a nutcase."
His gaze was too deep for such words... Jin wanted to say that, but he kept quiet, mindful of Syris's mood.
"Hmm, anyway, it makes sense if Talaris told you about this place. I mean, she remembered this place."
Quaul seemed to have a lot of questions about Talaris, but he kept them to himself.
Syris stepped aside, thinking he might draw his sword if he continued to observe Quaul.
Jin gave Quaul some time to gather his thoughts.
After a few minutes, Quaul's eyes were once again filled with caution. But it was much lighter than before.
"Next question. I get how you found out about this log cabin and the alias Tingjen Bower. But how did you know my real name?"
"My informants found out."
"I'll tell you in advance. If you joke or lie, the conversation ends right there."
"You're quite the stickler."

"Do you think Runcandel's information capabilities are superior to Zipfel's? Moreover, since you're only the 12th batch, your information power is not Runcandel's but Vamel Union's. I can't accept that you've figured out my real name to that extent."
Quaul's words implied one piece of information.
'Did Zipfel not know Quaul Ganesto, the real name of Tingjen Bower?'
How do you know something that even Zipfel doesn't know, Quaul was asking that.
"It's true that my informant found out your real name. The family doesn't even know about your existence or the fact that I'm looking for you."
It wasn't a lie to categorize Valeria simply as an informant, broadly speaking, she could also be classified as an informant of the Vamel Union.
Quaul stared at Jin for a while without saying a word.
"Hmm, it doesn't seem like you're lying."
That long eye contact was Quaul's own way of detecting lies. Although there seemed to be no solid evidence, it was not bad for Jin as he decided to let it go.
"I have a few questions too."
"Ask after I finish my questions."

"Why is a Zipfel engineer, even a figure central to the development of teleportation devices and mass production ship blueprints, stuck in such a remote place? Moreover, there doesn't even seem to be a single mage coming out to escort you, even in this situation."
Quaul wasn't as bothered by Jin's decision to ignore his words and ask a question.
He preferred this to the Zipfel rulers, who often showed their obsequious sides while carefully considering his mood.
Perhaps that small favor was a reward for reminding him of his forgotten old love, but Quaul vehemently denied this fact.

"Moreover, those rods that you seem to have made, they even have the ability to interfere with the aura focus of the unmanned. No matter how I think about it, it's strange that an engineer of your level is left in such a place."
"Abandoned? Did you say abandoned? Ha! You don't know me well. No one can bind me."
For some reason, at that moment, Jin thought of a black dragon he knew well.
'Murakan comes to mind...'
To put it nicely, this simple and unique, or rather, somewhat stupid and arrogant kind of people often showed an inability to let go when they got hooked on something.
Jin hoped that Quaul had such an element too.
"Zipfel released you, is that what you mean?"
"I was beginning to like you, but you keep scratching my pride. Zipfel? Those guys just coveted my abilities and temporarily had me in their custody. I was never part of them."
Jin had a rough idea.
'Zipfel can't handle this eccentric person freely. If he's a person who wouldn't cooperate at all if he offends him even a little, they would have no choice but to follow his will.'
There was absolutely nothing known in the world about Tingjen Bower, this arrogant genius engineer.
If Jin hadn't obtained some machine devices and ship blueprints in the Sota Desert, and if Valeria wasn't there, and if he wasn't related to Talaris, he probably wouldn't have come here.
Even if he did come, it would have been much later.
Also, Quaul has the ability to protect himself sufficiently against ordinary people, and Zipfel has been suffering from a severe power shortage since the Sword Emperor Temple incident.
'But even so, it's insufficient to explain why Quaul Ganesto is just left alone. Probably because the surname Ganesto is not yet known to Zipfel.'
Mind manipulation.
Suddenly, one of Zipfel's spells came to Jin's mind. At least so far, Quaul didn't seem to have been subjected to mind manipulation.
'Their mind manipulation isn't perfect yet, so if we exclude that, things roughly add up. And what was the reason Quaul was working with Zipfel in the first place?'
Even though Quaul Ganesto was not from the academy and his reputation was not known, it was clear that he was a genius engineer of a different dimension.
So it was quite possible that he had caught Zipfel's eye by demonstrating his abilities by chance.
'He's not the kind of person who would just get caught. If he needed advanced engineering equipment or resource support, he would have likely used the Academy first.'
Zipfel had made an attractive offer to Quaul.
The kind of offer that Quaul, who shudders at the thought of being bound, would temporarily ally himself with Zipfel.
Jin concluded as such.

"By any chance, did you work with Zipfel because there was something that piqued your interest? As a scholar, were you motivated by the development of things like teleportation devices or mass-produced ships?"
"Think whatever you want about that part."
It seemed like he was agreeing.
Normally, after hearing Quaul's answer, Jin would have felt a bit blocked.
Because there's no project that could surpass teleportation devices and mass-produced ships in the Runcandel-Vamel Alliance.
But now it's a different story.
He had the Mana Absorption Dispersion Cannon, a relic of the ancient past that Amela had confirmed to be a masterpiece, and he also had parts of a teleportation device and some ship blueprints.
In particular, the parts and blueprints were items that were clearly of great importance to Quaul.
"I'll ask you directly, Quaul Ganesto. If I could make an offer as attractive as Zipfel's, would you be willing to work with me?"
"There's no way that could be possible."
"Why not hear me out? Answer my question first, and if it matches your conditions, consider leaving the cabin?"

"I did say that, but I really don't expect much. If you're thinking of moving me through torture or something, go ahead. You'll just make yourselves the sinners of the world, setting back its progress by hundreds of years."
Jin didn't respond to that comment, but instead pulled out the mechanical device from his pocket and presented it to Quaul.
"I thought you might want to complete this device, but it seems I was mistaken."
Then Quaul's eyes widened as if they were about to pop out.
"What, what is this!? Why do you have this!?"
Jin couldn't help but smile triumphantly once again.
